item.title: Tupelo man arrested on aggravated domestic violence charge - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUPELO – A Tupelo man has been arrested and charged with aggravated domestic violence following an investigation by local authorities.

According to officials, officers first made contact with a victim on Feb. 20 at the North Mississippi Medical Center emergency room located at 830 South Gloster Street. The victim told officers she had been assaulted at a residence on Veterans Boulevard.

After further investigation, Tilar T. Thompson, 25, of Tupelo, was arrested on March 13 and charged with one count of aggravated domestic violence.

On March 15, Tupelo Municipal Court Judge Weir set Thompson’s bond at $40,000.

Authorities said the charge will be presented to the Lee County Grand Jury for further proceedings.

item.title: Trial begins today for Quinton Tellis in 2015 killing of Taiwanese exchange student - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MONROE, Louisiana — The murder trial for Quinton Tellis is happening today in Monroe, Louisiana after being rescheduled multiple times. This case has stretched on for nearly a decade.

Tellis is charged in Ouachita Parish with first-degree murder in the 2015 death of 34-year-old Meng-Chen Hsiao, a Taiwanese exchange student who was found tortured to death in Monroe, Louisiana.

The trial has been set to begin several times, most recently being postponed in December after the death of key expert witness Brigadier General Paul Rowlett, then again in January when ADA Holly Jones had the flue. Earlier this month, the trial was postponed again by the winter storm.

Tellis, 36, has long maintained his innocence in Hsiao’s death. Prosecutors allege he killed Hsiao in order to take her debit card. He pleaded guilty to using her card after he was caught on ATM cameras in Vicksburg.

The case has drawn national attention because Tellis was also charged in Mississippi with the 2014 burning death of Jessica Chambers in Panola County. He was tried twice in that case, but both trials ended in mistrials due to hung juries. It is unclear if he will be tried again by the state of Mississippi.

If convicted, Tellis could face a sentence of life in prison or the death penalty.

The proceedings are expected to take place in Ouachita Parish District Court.

Read previous stories on our coverage of Quinton Tellis here.

item.title: Tree falls on Natchez home during overnight storm, trapping occupants inside - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
NATCHEZ – A large tree fell onto a home in Natchez late Saturday night, causing major damage and temporarily trapping the occupants inside, according to the Adams County Sheriff’s Office.

Deputies said the incident happened around 11:30 p.m. March 15 in the 70 block of Mullins Road after a 911 caller reported that a tree had fallen onto the residence.

The caller told dispatchers the damage was significant and that the people inside could not safely get out of the home, authorities said.

When deputies arrived, they found that a large tree had fallen across the structure, causing structural damage and blocking access to the residence.

The Natchez Fire Department and AMR also responded to assist.

Emergency crews worked to secure the scene, help the occupants and assess the damage to the home. Officials said no serious injuries were reported.

The Adams County Sheriff’s Office reminded residents to use caution after severe weather, noting that fallen trees and debris can create dangerous conditions.

item.title: STEPPING UP TO SERVE: Deputies help rescue dog trapped after tree crushes car in Natchez - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
ADAMS COUNTY – Some heroes wear capes, but today’s heroes wear badges. They went above and beyond in a situation where they didn’t have to.

According to the Adams County Sheriff, a large tree fell onto a parked vehicle early Monday morning in Natchez, trapping a puppy underneath.

Deputies said they were called around 12:35 a.m. March 16 to a home in the 1500 block of Martin Luther King Jr. Street.

A 911 call was received reporting that a tree had fallen onto a vehicle in the yard of the home.

When deputies arrived, they found a large oak tree resting on top of a parked vehicle. The vehicle appeared to be disabled and was unoccupied at the time of the incident.

The caller also reported that a puppy had become trapped underneath the vehicle due to the weight of the tree pressing down on the car.

Deputies and responding personnel worked tirelessly to help to assess the situation and assist with efforts to safely remove the tree and free the terrified pup.

Thanks to the quick work of the Adams County deputies, nobody was injured. What could have been a terrible situation ended in a positive way.

Officials reminded residents to remain cautious following severe weather, noting that fallen trees and debris can create dangerous conditions for both people and property.

We are thankful for those who have compassion and choose to help even when it’s beyond their job description. These deputies are heroes and this family and the sweet puppy were definitely thankful.

item.title: Shaw Pit Bull Rescue seeks sponsors to help feed 23 dogs through March - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
COLUMBUS – Shaw Pit Bull Rescue is asking for the public’s help covering the cost of food for the dogs in its care this month.

The rescue, located in Columbus, said it currently feeds 23 dogs and goes through one full bag of dog food each day. With 31 days in March, that means the organization needs 31 bags of food to make it through the month.

According to the rescue, 19 bags have already been donated, covering 19 days in March. Supporters are now being asked to sponsor the remaining days.

The cost to sponsor one day of food is $48, which covers one full bag of food for all 23 dogs for that day.

The rescue said it uses Fromm Adult Gold dog food, which is available through Four Seasons Farm & Garden in Columbus. Supporters can donate a bag by calling the store at 662-329-2281 and designating it for Shaw Pit Bull Rescue.

Officials said the following days in March still need sponsors: March 3, 6, 8, 12, 14, 17, 19, 22, 25, 27, 29 and 31.

The rescue thanked the community for helping keep the dogs fed, healthy and cared for.

item.title: Rankin County deputies seize more than 2,000 kratom packets during investigation - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
RANKIN COUNTY – The Rankin County Sheriff’s Office has seized more than 2,000 packets of kratom from convenience stores following an investigation into the sale of the substance in unincorporated areas of the county.

According to the sheriff’s office, the investigation began after citizens reported complaints about kratom being sold at local convenience stores.

In March 2024, the Rankin County Board of Supervisors passed a county ordinance prohibiting the use, purchase, possession, distribution, sale or offering for sale of synthetic cocaine and kratom in unincorporated areas of Rankin County.

After the ordinance was approved, deputies hand-delivered copies of the new law to convenience stores across the county.

Investigators later conducted undercover purchases and audits of stores located in unincorporated areas of Rankin County.

The operation resulted in the seizure of approximately 2,030 packets of kratom, with an estimated value of $48,267.12, according to the sheriff’s office.

Store employees who allegedly sold kratom to undercover agents have been charged with violating the county ordinance. The violation carries a penalty of up to $1,000 in fines and/or up to six months in the county jail.

Authorities said the seized kratom products will be held as evidence until the cases are resolved and will then be destroyed.

The Rankin County Sheriff’s Office encourages residents to report stores selling illegal products in the county by calling 601-825-1480.

item.title: Pearl River County Sheriff’s Department introduces bloodhound trained for search and recovery - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
PEARL RIVER COUNTY – The Pearl River County Sheriff’s Department has introduced a new four-legged member of its team, a bloodhound trained to help locate missing persons and fugitives.

Amos, a 3-year-old bloodhound, has been trained in tracking and finding missing people as well as fugitive recovery, according to the sheriff’s department.

Officials said Capt. Shane Edgar traveled to Missouri to meet Amos and complete four days of training with him before bringing the dog back to Pearl River County. Since then, Amos has continued training in the county’s climate and terrain to prepare for local conditions, including heat, humidity and varied environments.

The sheriff’s department said Amos has already completed multiple successful tracks in a variety of locations and weather conditions.

Authorities said they are confident in Amos’ ability to work alongside deputies, the department’s Special Operations Team and Pearl River County JSAR.

Officials said Amos is expected to strengthen the department’s search and recovery efforts and improve its ability to support nearby and local agencies.

item.title: Oxford Police to host free women’s self-defense class Tuesday - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
OXFORD – The Oxford Police Department will host a free women’s self-defense class Tuesday evening at the department’s training room.

The class is scheduled for 6 p.m. on March 17 and will focus on practical, real-world techniques designed to improve awareness, build confidence and promote personal safety, according to the department.

Officials said the class is open to the public and no registration is required to attend.

The session will be held in the Oxford Police Department training room. While the class falls on St. Patrick’s Day, participants are encouraged to come ready to learn self-defense skills. Wearing green is optional, the department said.

Oxford police said the class is part of the department’s ongoing efforts to promote community safety and personal preparedness.

item.title: Operation Check Mate leads to 30 arrests, drug and firearm seizures in Meridian - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
MERIDIAN – Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch announced the completion of Operation Check Mate, a multi-agency law enforcement effort led by the Attorney General’s Office Fentanyl Strike Force.

According to Fitch’s office, the operation resulted in 20 felony arrests, 10 misdemeanor arrests, one DUI, 156 traffic citations and the execution of one search warrant.

“Fighting the fentanyl epidemic cannot be done without cooperation. It takes all of us,” Fitch said in a statement. “My office is committed to building a network of law enforcement across the state with the tools and knowledge to disrupt drug operations and successfully prosecute these criminals. Thank you to our local, state and federal partners who worked with us during this operation. Together, we can get these dangerous criminals out of our communities and drugs off of our streets.”

During the operation, law enforcement officers seized four firearms, marijuana, methamphetamine, MDMA pills, crack cocaine, suspected fentanyl powder, $7,368 in suspected illicit proceeds and 40 illegal gambling devices.

Participating agencies included the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Lauderdale County Sheriff’s Department, the Meridian Police Department, Mississippi Alcoholic Beverage Control, the Mississippi Bureau of Narcotics, the Mississippi Gaming Commission and the Naval Criminal Investigative Service.

Fitch created the Fentanyl Strike Force in 2023 as part of the rollout of the One Pill Can Kill public education and awareness campaign.

Officials said Operation Check Mate followed one of the free Fentanyl Strike Force training sessions offered by the Attorney General’s Office. More than 800 officers have now been trained in narcotics investigations, as well as in the use of naloxone and fentanyl test strips.

Law enforcement agencies interested in participating in the Fentanyl Strike Force can contact the Attorney General’s Office at [email protected] .

item.title: MISSING IN MISSISSIPPI: John Doe, Calhoun County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
CALHOUN COUNTY — Nearly nine years after a human skull was discovered in rural Calhoun County, investigators are still searching for answers about the unidentified man and how he died.

Authorities say the cranium of a male was found May 4, 2017, prompting a search of approximately 45 acres in the surrounding area. Despite the extensive search, no additional human remains were located.

Officials initially said the remains were believed to belong to a Hispanic male, but investigators have been unable to determine the man’s age, height or weight.

Sheriff Greg Pollan previously said the case has produced very few leads since the discovery, leaving authorities with little information about the victim’s identity.

Recent forensic genetic genealogy work has provided new clues. DNA analysis indicates the man likely had Mexican and Iberian Peninsula ancestry, and investigators believe someone may recognize him.

However, officials say the search has been complicated by the scarcity of Hispanic and Latino DNA profiles in the databases used for forensic genealogy, including DNASolves, FamilyTreeDNA and GEDmatch.

Investigators are asking for the public’s help in two ways. First, they encourage people to share information about the case on social media, which could lead to new tips or recognition.

Second, individuals of Hispanic or Latino descent who have taken consumer DNA tests are encouraged to upload their results to FamilyTreeDNA or GEDmatch, where they may help generate investigative leads.

Common surnames appearing in DNA matches include Martinez, Serna and Ledesma, with ancestral ties to Nuevo León and San Luis Potosí, Mexico.

Authorities say people with family connections to those areas who have taken DNA tests could play a key role in helping identify the man.

An artist’s rendering has also been created to show what the victim may have looked like in hopes that someone might recognize him.

The case remains under investigation by the Calhoun County Medical Examiner’s Office. Anyone with information that could help identify the victim is asked to contact the office at 662-628-5177.

item.title: Man wanted on 16 felony cases in Neshoba County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Cash Matlock
item.description:
NESHOBA COUNTY – The Neshoba County Sheriff’s Office is asking for the public’s help locating a man wanted on multiple felony charges.

Investigators say Reginald Demondra Triplett, 55, is wanted on a circuit court bench warrant related to 16 pending felony cases in Neshoba County.

Triplett, whose date of birth is listed as Dec. 8, 1970, is currently being sought by the sheriff’s office, according to a post on the Neshoba County Sheriff’s Office Facebook page.

Anyone with information about Triplett’s whereabouts is encouraged to contact East Mississippi Crime Stoppers at 1-855-485-8477. Callers may be eligible for a cash reward if the information leads to an arrest.

No additional details about the pending cases were immediately released.

item.title: Interview videos highlight apparent inconsistencies in Quinton Tellis's stories in Louisiana trial - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MONROE, La. — An almost physical chill passed through Judge Larry Jefferson’s courtroom in the Ouachita Parish Courthouse in Louisiana on Monday when Quinton Tellis said in a taped interview, “I’m not a murderer. I’m not a murderer!”

If Tellis told Louisiana investigators, “I’ve got no reason to lie to you,” or “I’m telling the truth” once during his 2015 interviews after the brutal stabbing of Ming Chen “Mandy” Hsiao, he said it 1,000 times.

The interviews took place after the 2015 death of Hsiao and during the investigation into the 2014 death of Jessica Chambers in Panola County, Mississippi, in which he was the prime suspect. Over a decade later with hindsight, the videos seemed to carry infinitely more meaning than they might have at the time.

The first day of testimony centered on what investigators say were many versions of events he gave them in the days after Hsiao’s death.

The bench trial began Monday in the courtroom of Larry Jefferson, where Assistant District Attorney Holly Jones used recorded police interviews from the time of the homicide to highlight apparent inconsistencies in Tellis’ statements.

Hsiao, a Taiwanese national living in Monroe, was found stabbed to death on Aug. 8, 2015, which was Tellis’s wedding day.

Throughout the interview recordings played in court, Tellis repeatedly insisted he was telling the truth. At several points he told investigators, “I’m not lying,” a phrase he repeated again and again during questioning.

Prosecutors introduced two sets of interviews conducted on Aug. 11 and Aug. 19, 2015. The recordings were shown as part of testimony from Duane Cookson, a Monroe police sergeant who took the stand to explain the circumstances surrounding the interviews.

Cookson testified that he and investigator Jeremy Kent conducted much of the questioning shown in the videos.

As Tellis first entered the interview room, investigators mentioned for the camera that they had told him it was about a homicide, and that he had asked, “What does homicide mean?”

During the interviews, prosecutors argued, Tellis’ account of what happened in the days surrounding Hsiao’s death seemed to shift multiple times. His first story was that he and his stepson had met Hsiao because she would ride her bike with the neighborhood children. Detectives showed skepticism that a 34-year-old woman was riding bikes with children, and then asked Tellis how he ended up in the car with her at Walmart.

She had a prescription for some lortabs, he said, so he told them he had taken her to pick it up so she could sell it to him. He said he gave her $50 for that and a television. At some point, he told investigators that she had a boyfriend, but that he didn’t know him and had never seen him.

Shortly after that, he said he had given her $50 for the lortabs and another $25 for the television, and that when he had gone to her apartment to pick it up with his 8-year-old stepson and another neighborhood child, she hadn’t been there. They had seen “a white girl” who had told them that Mandy wasn’t there, even though her bike was there, Tellis said.

Witnesses had told investigators at the time that they heard Tellis and Hsiao arguing in the parking lot, they said, and Tellis held fast that he wasn’t there and that he never argued with Hsiao, with whom he said he did not have a sexual relationship. He did admit to at least one relationship he had outside of the one he had with his new wife, Chakita Jackson, but it was not with Hsiao.

Investigators asked him how long he had known Hsiao before taking her to Walmart to pick up the prescription, and he said it had been just about a week. Again, detectives appeared skeptical, pressing him on how he met a woman who was riding bikes and suddenly was taking her to Walmart so he could buy her prescription drugs.

Tellis told the story as if he felt it wasn’t strange, and that she had just told him during the course of conversation that she had the prescription and needed money for a microwave. Another confusing rabbit trail in Tellis’ interview was when he told investigators that he took Jackson with him to look for a microwave for Hsiao even though they had one.

He had sold the lortabs to “some white guys,” Tellis told investigators.

At one point, Kent raised his voice as he questioned Tellis.

“Why is she dead?” he demanded, and Tellis said, “I don’t know. That’s something I don’t understand.”

Investigators asked if it might have been that Tellis felt like Hsiao had cheated him on the $25 for the TV she was supposed to be selling him since she allegedly wasn’t home when he went to collect it.

At that point, Tellis told detectives that Hsiao had a boyfriend. As his story wandered, investigators became more frustrated. When they asked him how it was possible that everyone was lying except him, he said, “I don’t know, but they are. I’m not lying, right hand to God.”

“God’s not here to testify,” Kent said.

The interviews were hard to hear from the spectator section of the courtroom, but at one point they turned the questioning to someone Tellis called “Jay.” They had been to the Chase bank together, Tellis said.

Jay became a central figure, and as investigators introduced evidence they had of Tellis using Hsiao’s debit card, Tellis first said he got it from Jay.

“I’ve gotta break this to you,” one of the investigators told him. “Life as you know it is about to change. I know for a fact you’ve given us some lies, and you’ve brought people into these lies.”

“I don’t believe you,” Kent said. “Everything you’ve said is a lie.”

“Don’t say that,” Tellis replied. “I aint never killed anybody. I’m not a murderer.”

item.title: Highway Patrol, Lee County deputies issue 78 citations in school zone enforcement operation - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
LEE COUNTY – A traffic enforcement operation near Shannon Primary School resulted in 78 citations and two DUI arrests, according to Lee County Sheriff Jim H. Johnson.

Johnson said he coordinated with the Mississippi Highway Patrol last week to focus enforcement on Highway 45 near the school zone after recent safety concerns in school areas.

He said saturation patrols were requested in the area to increase awareness and cite drivers violating traffic laws.

During the operation, officials issued 78 citations, all during active school hours in the school zone. Authorities also made two arrests for driving under the influence.

Johnson said the goal of the enforcement effort was to protect children and improve safety in the school zone.

Officials are reminding drivers to slow down, stay alert and obey traffic laws when traveling through school zones.

item.title: Gautier man arrested in child sexual battery investigation - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
GAUTIER – A Gautier man has been arrested and charged in a child sexual battery investigation, according to the Gautier Police Department.

Police said officers arrested Travis Wilson, 37, on Friday, March 15, and charged him with sexual battery of a child under the age of 14.

Wilson is being held at the Jackson County Adult Detention Center. Authorities said he is scheduled to make his initial appearance in Gautier Municipal Court on March 16.

Police said the investigation remains ongoing and additional charges are possible as investigators continue gathering information.

Anyone with information related to the case is asked to contact the Gautier Police Department Investigations Division at 228-497-2486.

Anonymous tips can also be submitted through Mississippi Coast Crime Stoppers by calling 877-787-5898 or through the P3 Tips app.

item.title: Freedom of Information Day highlights public’s right to know - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
STATEWIDE — Americans mark Freedom of Information Day each year on March 16, celebrating the public’s right to access government records and the principle of transparency in democracy.

The date honors the birthday of James Madison, widely known as the “Father of the Constitution” and a strong advocate for open government. Observed nationwide, the day highlights laws and policies that allow citizens to obtain information about how government agencies operate.

The observance is closely tied to the Freedom of Information Act, a federal law passed in 1966 that gives the public the right to request records from federal agencies. The law allows individuals to access government documents related to decisions, operations and other official activities, typically at little or no cost.

Supporters say the law is one of the most important tools for government accountability, allowing journalists, researchers and everyday citizens to examine how public officials conduct the nation’s business, so if your lawmaker or government organization is giving you a hard time accessing those records, remind them the very framework of our country demands it.

Freedom of Information Day also serves as an opportunity to recognize individuals and groups who advocate for transparency. The American Library Association presents the James Madison Award each year to honor people or organizations that promote public access to government information, along with the Eileen Cooke State and Local Madison Award recognizing grassroots efforts to protect the public’s right to know.

Every state also has its own version of an open records law. In Mississippi, that law is the Mississippi Public Records Act, enacted in 1983. The law allows anyone to inspect or copy most records held by state and local government agencies, including documents, emails, photographs and recordings used in the course of public business.

The Mississippi law generally requires agencies to respond to public records requests within seven working days. If a request cannot be fulfilled within that timeframe, the agency must provide a written explanation and typically must produce the records within 14 working days unless special circumstances apply.

While most records are open, the law includes exemptions to protect certain types of sensitive information, including some personal data, medical records, personnel files and certain law enforcement records.

Transparency advocates say open records laws are a cornerstone of democracy, giving citizens the tools to hold their government accountable.

The observance each March serves as a reminder of Madison’s belief that access to information is essential to a functioning democracy, and that informed citizens play a crucial role in ensuring government remains accountable to the public.

item.title: Capitol Police investigating crash after brief pursuit in Jackson - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Capitol Police are investigating after a vehicle overturned following a brief pursuit Saturday evening in Jackson.

According to authorities, officers attempted to initiate a traffic stop around 6:58 p.m. on March 14 near Sunset Drive for traffic violations.

Police said the driver failed to yield, leading officers on a brief pursuit that ended near Eubanks Creek when the vehicle overturned.

One person fled the scene on foot, authorities said. Three others were arrested at the scene without further incident.

Officials said charges are pending. The investigation remains open and ongoing.

item.title: 21-year-old inmate charged with murder dies in custody at Jones County jail - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JONES COUNTY – A 21-year-old inmate charged with murder died Monday after being found unresponsive inside the Jones County Adult Detention Facility, according to Jones County Sheriff Joe Berlin.

Sheriff Berlin said Nehemiah Rice was booked into the detention center on March 16 on a murder charge filed by the Ellisville Police Department in connection with a shooting at an Ellisville hotel.

Authorities said Rice was interviewed by an Ellisville Police Department investigator in an interview room at the detention facility. After the interview was completed, the investigator left the jail and Rice was returned to his cell.

According to the sheriff’s office, Rice was later discovered unresponsive in his cell. Corrections officers administered CPR and nasal Narcan while emergency medical services were dispatched.

EMServ Ambulance Service responded and transported Rice to South Central Regional Medical Center while continuing life-saving efforts. Rice was later pronounced dead.

The Mississippi Bureau of Investigation has been contacted to conduct an investigation into the incident, which officials described as an “in-custody” death until an official determination is made.

item.title: Terry police seek two suspects in Maxie Street shooting - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
TERRY — The Terry Police Department is asking for the public’s help in locating two individuals wanted in connection with an aggravated assault following a shooting Thursday night.

Police said officers were notified March 12, 2026, of a shooting in the 1100 block of Maxie Street. One person sustained injuries that were not considered life-threatening.

Authorities said Kameka Henry and La’Quan Moore are wanted in connection with the incident.

Anyone with information about the whereabouts of the two individuals is asked to contact the Terry Police Department at 601-878-5521.

The case remains under investigation.

item.title: Pontotoc man arrested on meth charge after Lee County traffic stop - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
LEE COUNTY – Deputies with the Lee County Sheriff’s Office arrested a Pontotoc man on a methamphetamine charge following a traffic stop in the Shannon area.

Sheriff Jim H. Johnson said the stop took place March 12. During the encounter, deputies found the driver to be in possession of methamphetamine.

Authorities identified the suspect as Christopher L. Tedford, 48, of Pontotoc.

A Lee County Justice Court judge set Tedford’s bond at $25,000.

item.title: Missing and endangered alert issued for 17-year-old Copiah County girl with severe seizures - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
COPIAH COUNTY – The Mississippi Bureau of Investigation has issued a missing and endangered notification for a 17-year-old girl from Hazlehurst.

Authorities identified the teen as Ariel Elise Charday Davis. She is described as 5 feet 3 inches tall, weighing about 260 pounds, with black hair and brown eyes.

According to investigators, Davis was last seen Tuesday, March 10, at about 9:11 a.m. at her home in Copiah County.

The alert was issued by the Mississippi Bureau of Investigation on behalf of the Copiah County Sheriff’s Office.

Family members told authorities that Davis has a history of severe seizures.

Anyone who sees Davis or has information about her whereabouts is asked to contact the Copiah County Sheriff’s Office at 601-953-9932 or call 911.

item.title: Hancock County authorities seek man wanted on assault warrant - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
HANCOCK COUNTY – The Hancock County Sheriff’s Office is asking for the public’s help locating a man wanted on a warrant for simple assault.

Authorities are searching for Gary Lynn Sanders, who is described as approximately 6 feet 1 inch tall and weighing about 250 pounds.

Investigators said Sanders is known to ride a Harley-Davidson motorcycle and has been seen wearing patches associated with the Galloping Goose Motorcycle Club.

According to the sheriff’s office, Sanders is known to frequent Pearl River County in Mississippi as well as Jefferson and St. Tammany parishes in Louisiana.

Anyone with information about Sanders’ whereabouts is asked to contact Crime Stoppers by using the P3 Tips app or by dialing **TIPS. Officials said tips must be submitted directly through Crime Stoppers to be eligible for a reward.

Authorities noted that all persons are considered innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

item.title: Tunica deputies ask public to identify drivers of stolen vehicle - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUNICA COUNTY – The Tunica County Sheriff’s Office is asking for the public’s help identifying the drivers of a vehicle that was recently reported stolen and may be connected to a shooting in the area.

According to the sheriff’s office, the vehicle was reported stolen out of Tunica County and is believed to have been driven by suspects involved in a shooting that occurred recently in the White Oak area.

Investigators are working to identify the individuals who were operating the vehicle at the time of the incident and are urging anyone who may recognize the vehicle or its drivers to come forward.

Anyone with information is asked to contact the Tunica County Sheriff’s Office at 662-363-1411 to speak with an investigator. Tips can also be submitted anonymously through CrimeStoppers at 662-910-0400.

Authorities said information leading to an arrest may be eligible for a reward of up to $1,000.

The investigation remains ongoing.
